I thought thy bride-bed to have deck’d, sweet maid,
And not have strew’d thy grave.
speeches.stage: [_Scattering flowers._] Sweets to the sweet. Farewell.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: O, treble woe
Fall ten times treble on that cursed head
Whose wicked deed thy most ingenious sense
Depriv’d thee of. Hold off the earth a while,
Till I have caught her once more in mine arms.
[_Leaps into the grave._]
Now pile your dust upon the quick and dead,
Till of this flat a mountain you have made,
To o’ertop old Pelion or the skyish head
Of blue Olympus.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: What is he whose grief
Bears such an emphasis? whose phrase of sorrow
Conjures the wand’ring stars, and makes them stand
Like wonder-wounded hearers? This is I,
Hamlet the Dane.
[_Leaps into the grave._]

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.stage: [_Grappling with him._] The devil take thy soul!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Thou pray’st not well.
I prithee take thy fingers from my throat;
For though I am not splenative and rash,
Yet have I in me something dangerous,
Which let thy wiseness fear. Away thy hand!

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Pluck them asunder.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: Hamlet! Hamlet!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Good my lord, be quiet.

speeches.stage: [_The Attendants part them, and they come out of the grave._]

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Why, I will fight with him upon this theme
Until my eyelids will no longer wag.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: O my son, what theme?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I lov’d Ophelia; forty thousand brothers
Could not, with all their quantity of love,
Make up my sum. What wilt thou do for her?

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: O, he is mad, Laertes.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: For love of God forbear him!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: ’Swounds, show me what thou’lt do:
Woul’t weep? woul’t fight? woul’t fast? woul’t tear thyself?
Woul’t drink up eisel? eat a crocodile?
I’ll do’t. Dost thou come here to whine?
To outface me with leaping in her grave?
Be buried quick with her, and so will I.
And if thou prate of mountains, let them throw
Millions of acres on us, till our ground,
Singeing his pate against the burning zone,
Make Ossa like a wart. Nay, an thou’lt mouth,
I’ll rant as well as thou.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: This is mere madness:
And thus awhile the fit will work on him;
Anon, as patient as the female dove,
When that her golden couplets are disclos’d,
His silence will sit drooping.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Hear you, sir;
What is the reason that you use me thus?
I lov’d you ever. But it is no matter.
Let Hercules himself do what he may,
The cat will mew, and dog will have his day.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: I pray thee, good Horatio, wait upon him.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: So much for this, sir. Now let me see the other;
You do remember all the circumstance?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Remember it, my lord!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Sir, in my heart there was a kind of fighting
That would not let me sleep. Methought I lay
Worse than the mutinies in the bilboes. Rashly,
And prais’d be rashness for it,—let us know,
Our indiscretion sometime serves us well,
When our deep plots do pall; and that should teach us
There’s a divinity that shapes our ends,
Rough-hew them how we will.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: That is most certain.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Up from my cabin,
My sea-gown scarf’d about me, in the dark
Grop’d I to find out them; had my desire,
Finger’d their packet, and in fine, withdrew
To mine own room again, making so bold,
My fears forgetting manners, to unseal
Their grand commission; where I found, Horatio,
Oh royal knavery! an exact command,
Larded with many several sorts of reasons,
Importing Denmark’s health, and England’s too,
With ho! such bugs and goblins in my life,
That on the supervise, no leisure bated,
No, not to stay the grinding of the axe,
My head should be struck off.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Is’t possible?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Here’s the commission, read it at more leisure.
But wilt thou hear me how I did proceed?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: I beseech you.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Being thus benetted round with villanies,—
Or I could make a prologue to my brains,
They had begun the play,—I sat me down,
Devis’d a new commission, wrote it fair:
I once did hold it, as our statists do,
A baseness to write fair, and labour’d much
How to forget that learning; but, sir, now
It did me yeoman’s service. Wilt thou know
The effect of what I wrote?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Ay, good my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: An earnest conjuration from the King,
As England was his faithful tributary,
As love between them like the palm might flourish,
As peace should still her wheaten garland wear
And stand a comma ’tween their amities,
And many such-like ‘as’es of great charge,
That on the view and know of these contents,
Without debatement further, more or less,
He should the bearers put to sudden death,
Not shriving-time allow’d.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: How was this seal’d?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Why, even in that was heaven ordinant.
I had my father’s signet in my purse,
Which was the model of that Danish seal:
Folded the writ up in the form of the other,
Subscrib’d it: gave’t th’impression; plac’d it safely,
The changeling never known. Now, the next day
Was our sea-fight, and what to this was sequent
Thou know’st already.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: So Guildenstern and Rosencrantz go to’t.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Why, man, they did make love to this employment.
They are not near my conscience; their defeat
Does by their own insinuation grow.
’Tis dangerous when the baser nature comes
Between the pass and fell incensed points
Of mighty opposites.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Why, what a king is this!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Does it not, thinks’t thee, stand me now upon,—
He that hath kill’d my king, and whor’d my mother,
Popp’d in between th’election and my hopes,
Thrown out his angle for my proper life,
And with such cozenage—is’t not perfect conscience
To quit him with this arm? And is’t not to be damn’d
To let this canker of our nature come
In further evil?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: It must be shortly known to him from England
What is the issue of the business there.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: It will be short. The interim is mine;
And a man’s life’s no more than to say ‘One’.
But I am very sorry, good Horatio,
That to Laertes I forgot myself;
For by the image of my cause I see
The portraiture of his. I’ll court his favours.
But sure the bravery of his grief did put me
Into a tow’ring passion.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Peace, who comes here?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Your lordship is right welcome back to Denmark.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I humbly thank you, sir. Dost know this waterfly?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: No, my good lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Thy state is the more gracious; for ’tis a vice to know him. He hath
much land, and fertile; let a beast be lord of beasts, and his crib
shall stand at the king’s mess; ’tis a chough; but, as I say, spacious
in the possession of dirt.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Sweet lord, if your lordship were at leisure, I should impart a thing
to you from his Majesty.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I will receive it with all diligence of spirit. Put your bonnet to his
right use; ’tis for the head.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: I thank your lordship, ’tis very hot.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: No, believe me, ’tis very cold, the wind is northerly.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: It is indifferent cold, my lord, indeed.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Methinks it is very sultry and hot for my complexion.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Exceedingly, my lord; it is very sultry,—as ’twere—I cannot tell how.
But, my lord, his Majesty bade me signify to you that he has laid a
great wager on your head. Sir, this is the matter,—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I beseech you, remember,—

speeches.stage: [_Hamlet moves him to put on his hat._]

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Nay, in good faith; for mine ease, in good faith. Sir, here is newly
come to court Laertes; believe me, an absolute gentleman, full of most
excellent differences, of very soft society and great showing. Indeed,
to speak feelingly of him, he is the card or calendar of gentry; for
you shall find in him the continent of what part a gentleman would see.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Sir, his definement suffers no perdition in you, though I know, to
divide him inventorially would dizzy th’arithmetic of memory, and yet
but yaw neither, in respect of his quick sail. But, in the verity of
extolment, I take him to be a soul of great article and his infusion of
such dearth and rareness as, to make true diction of him, his semblable
is his mirror and who else would trace him his umbrage, nothing more.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Your lordship speaks most infallibly of him.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: The concernancy, sir? Why do we wrap the gentleman in our more rawer
breath?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Sir?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Is’t not possible to understand in another tongue? You will do’t, sir,
really.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: What imports the nomination of this gentleman?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Of Laertes?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: His purse is empty already, all’s golden words are spent.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Of him, sir.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: I know you are not ignorant,—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I would you did, sir; yet in faith if you did, it would not much
approve me. Well, sir?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: You are not ignorant of what excellence Laertes is,—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I dare not confess that, lest I should compare with him in excellence;
but to know a man well were to know himself.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: I mean, sir, for his weapon; but in the imputation laid on him, by them
in his meed he’s unfellowed.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: What’s his weapon?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Rapier and dagger.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: That’s two of his weapons. But well.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: The King, sir, hath wager’d with him six Barbary horses, against the
which he has imponed, as I take it, six French rapiers and poniards,
with their assigns, as girdle, hangers, and so. Three of the carriages,
in faith, are very dear to fancy, very responsive to the hilts, most
delicate carriages, and of very liberal conceit.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: What call you the carriages?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: I knew you must be edified by the margin ere you had done.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: The carriages, sir, are the hangers.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: The phrase would be more german to the matter if we could carry cannon
by our sides. I would it might be hangers till then. But on. Six
Barbary horses against six French swords, their assigns, and three
liberal conceited carriages: that’s the French bet against the Danish.
Why is this all imponed, as you call it?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: The King, sir, hath laid that in a dozen passes between you and him, he
shall not exceed you three hits. He hath laid on twelve for nine. And
it would come to immediate trial if your lordship would vouchsafe the
answer.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: How if I answer no?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: I mean, my lord, the opposition of your person in trial.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Sir, I will walk here in the hall. If it please his Majesty, it is the
breathing time of day with me. Let the foils be brought, the gentleman
willing, and the King hold his purpose, I will win for him if I can; if
not, I will gain nothing but my shame and the odd hits.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Shall I re-deliver you e’en so?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: To this effect, sir; after what flourish your nature will.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: I commend my duty to your lordship.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Yours, yours.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: This lapwing runs away with the shell on his head.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: He did comply with his dug before he suck’d it. Thus has he,—and many
more of the same bevy that I know the drossy age dotes on,— only got
the tune of the time and outward habit of encounter; a kind of yeasty
collection, which carries them through and through the most fanned and
winnowed opinions; and do but blow them to their trial, the bubbles are
out.

speeches.speaker: LORD
lines: My lord, his Majesty commended him to you by young Osric, who brings
back to him that you attend him in the hall. He sends to know if your
pleasure hold to play with Laertes or that you will take longer time.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I am constant to my purposes, they follow the King’s pleasure. If his
fitness speaks, mine is ready. Now or whensoever, provided I be so able
as now.

speeches.speaker: LORD
lines: The King and Queen and all are coming down.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: In happy time.

speeches.speaker: LORD
lines: The Queen desires you to use some gentle entertainment to Laertes
before you fall to play.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: She well instructs me.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: You will lose this wager, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I do not think so. Since he went into France, I have been in continual
practice. I shall win at the odds. But thou wouldst not think how ill
all’s here about my heart: but it is no matter.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Nay, good my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: It is but foolery; but it is such a kind of gain-giving as would
perhaps trouble a woman.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: If your mind dislike anything, obey it. I will forestall their repair
hither, and say you are not fit.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Not a whit, we defy augury. There’s a special providence in the fall of
a sparrow. If it be now, ’tis not to come; if it be not to come, it
will be now; if it be not now, yet it will come. The readiness is all.
Since no man has aught of what he leaves, what is’t to leave betimes?

speeches.stage: Enter King, Queen, Laertes, Lords, Osric and Attendants with foils &c.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Come, Hamlet, come, and take this hand from me.

speeches.stage: [_The King puts Laertes’s hand into Hamlet’s._]

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Give me your pardon, sir. I have done you wrong;
But pardon’t as you are a gentleman.
This presence knows, and you must needs have heard,
How I am punish’d with sore distraction.
What I have done
That might your nature, honour, and exception
Roughly awake, I here proclaim was madness.
Was’t Hamlet wrong’d Laertes? Never Hamlet.
If Hamlet from himself be ta’en away,
And when he’s not himself does wrong Laertes,
Then Hamlet does it not, Hamlet denies it.
Who does it, then? His madness. If’t be so,
Hamlet is of the faction that is wrong’d;
His madness is poor Hamlet’s enemy.
Sir, in this audience,
Let my disclaiming from a purpos’d evil
Free me so far in your most generous thoughts
That I have shot my arrow o’er the house
And hurt my brother.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: I am satisfied in nature,
Whose motive in this case should stir me most
To my revenge. But in my terms of honour
I stand aloof, and will no reconcilement
Till by some elder masters of known honour
I have a voice and precedent of peace
To keep my name ungor’d. But till that time
I do receive your offer’d love like love,
And will not wrong it.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I embrace it freely,
And will this brother’s wager frankly play.—
Give us the foils; come on.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Come, one for me.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I’ll be your foil, Laertes; in mine ignorance
Your skill shall like a star i’ th’ darkest night,
Stick fiery off indeed.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: You mock me, sir.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: No, by this hand.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Give them the foils, young Osric. Cousin Hamlet,
You know the wager?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Very well, my lord.
Your Grace has laid the odds o’ the weaker side.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: I do not fear it. I have seen you both;
But since he is better’d, we have therefore odds.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: This is too heavy. Let me see another.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: This likes me well. These foils have all a length?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Ay, my good lord.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Set me the stoups of wine upon that table.
If Hamlet give the first or second hit,
Or quit in answer of the third exchange,
Let all the battlements their ordnance fire;
The King shall drink to Hamlet’s better breath,
And in the cup an union shall he throw
Richer than that which four successive kings
In Denmark’s crown have worn. Give me the cups;
And let the kettle to the trumpet speak,
The trumpet to the cannoneer without,
The cannons to the heavens, the heavens to earth,
‘Now the King drinks to Hamlet.’ Come, begin.
And you, the judges, bear a wary eye.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Come on, sir.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Come, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: One.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: No.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Judgement.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: A hit, a very palpable hit.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Well; again.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Stay, give me drink. Hamlet, this pearl is thine;
Here’s to thy health.

speeches.stage: [_Trumpets sound, and cannon shot off within._]

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I’ll play this bout first; set it by awhile.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: A touch, a touch, I do confess.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Our son shall win.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: He’s fat, and scant of breath.
Here, Hamlet, take my napkin, rub thy brows.
The Queen carouses to thy fortune, Hamlet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Good madam.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Gertrude, do not drink.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: I will, my lord; I pray you pardon me.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.stage: [_Aside._] It is the poison’d cup; it is too late.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: I dare not drink yet, madam. By and by.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: Come, let me wipe thy face.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: My lord, I’ll hit him now.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: I do not think’t.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Come for the third, Laertes. You do but dally.
I pray you pass with your best violence.
I am afeard you make a wanton of me.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Say you so? Come on.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Nothing neither way.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Have at you now.

speeches.stage: [_Laertes wounds Hamlet; then, in scuffling, they change rapiers, and

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: Part them; they are incens’d.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Nay, come again!

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Look to the Queen there, ho!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: They bleed on both sides. How is it, my lord?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: How is’t, Laertes?

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: Why, as a woodcock to my own springe, Osric.
I am justly kill’d with mine own treachery.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: How does the Queen?

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: She swoons to see them bleed.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
lines: No, no, the drink, the drink! O my dear Hamlet!
The drink, the drink! I am poison’d.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: O villany! Ho! Let the door be lock’d:
Treachery! Seek it out.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: It is here, Hamlet. Hamlet, thou art slain.
No medicine in the world can do thee good.
In thee there is not half an hour of life;
The treacherous instrument is in thy hand,
Unbated and envenom’d. The foul practice
Hath turn’d itself on me. Lo, here I lie,
Never to rise again. Thy mother’s poison’d.
I can no more. The King, the King’s to blame.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: The point envenom’d too!
Then, venom, to thy work.

speeches.speaker: KING
lines: O yet defend me, friends. I am but hurt.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Here, thou incestuous, murderous, damned Dane,
Drink off this potion. Is thy union here?
Follow my mother.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
lines: He is justly serv’d.
It is a poison temper’d by himself.
Exchange forgiveness with me, noble Hamlet.
Mine and my father’s death come not upon thee,
Nor thine on me.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: Heaven make thee free of it! I follow thee.
I am dead, Horatio. Wretched Queen, adieu.
You that look pale and tremble at this chance,
That are but mutes or audience to this act,
Had I but time,—as this fell sergeant, death,
Is strict in his arrest,—O, I could tell you,—
But let it be. Horatio, I am dead,
Thou liv’st; report me and my cause aright
To the unsatisfied.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Never believe it.
I am more an antique Roman than a Dane.
Here’s yet some liquor left.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: As th’art a man,
Give me the cup. Let go; by Heaven, I’ll have’t.
O good Horatio, what a wounded name,
Things standing thus unknown, shall live behind me.
If thou didst ever hold me in thy heart,
Absent thee from felicity awhile,
And in this harsh world draw thy breath in pain,
To tell my story.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
lines: Young Fortinbras, with conquest come from Poland,
To the ambassadors of England gives
This warlike volley.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
lines: O, I die, Horatio.
The potent poison quite o’er-crows my spirit:
I cannot live to hear the news from England,
But I do prophesy th’election lights
On Fortinbras. He has my dying voice.
So tell him, with the occurrents more and less,
Which have solicited. The rest is silence.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince,
And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
Why does the drum come hither?

speeches.stage: Enter Fortinbras, the English Ambassadors and others.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
lines: Where is this sight?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: What is it you would see?
If aught of woe or wonder, cease your search.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
lines: This quarry cries on havoc. O proud death,
What feast is toward in thine eternal cell,
That thou so many princes at a shot
So bloodily hast struck?

speeches.speaker: FIRST AMBASSADOR
lines: The sight is dismal;
And our affairs from England come too late.
The ears are senseless that should give us hearing,
To tell him his commandment is fulfill’d,
That Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are dead.
Where should we have our thanks?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Not from his mouth,
Had it th’ability of life to thank you.
He never gave commandment for their death.
But since, so jump upon this bloody question,
You from the Polack wars, and you from England
Are here arriv’d, give order that these bodies
High on a stage be placed to the view,
And let me speak to th’ yet unknowing world
How these things came about. So shall you hear
Of carnal, bloody and unnatural acts,
Of accidental judgements, casual slaughters,
Of deaths put on by cunning and forc’d cause,
And, in this upshot, purposes mistook
Fall’n on the inventors’ heads. All this can I
Truly deliver.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
lines: Let us haste to hear it,
And call the noblest to the audience.
For me, with sorrow I embrace my fortune.
I have some rights of memory in this kingdom,
Which now to claim my vantage doth invite me.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
lines: Of that I shall have also cause to speak,
And from his mouth whose voice will draw on more.
But let this same be presently perform’d,
Even while men’s minds are wild, lest more mischance
On plots and errors happen.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
lines: Let four captains
Bear Hamlet like a soldier to the stage,
For he was likely, had he been put on,
To have prov’d most royally; and for his passage,
The soldiers’ music and the rites of war
Speak loudly for him.
Take up the bodies. Such a sight as this
Becomes the field, but here shows much amiss.
Go, bid the soldiers shoot.
